items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: He and Jeff Hamilton and Dennis Mackrel and Steve Houghton, and all these great drummers I’ve gotten to play with.

ctx.x: I’m going to backtrack a little bit. You talked about when you got to Eastman you needed to bone up on your theory some, and get more informed about that. Do you think it changed the way you improvised?

Yes, I feel it’s continuing to. I just, I sort of consider myself an ear player to a degree, but I want to be an informed ear player. I mean so I know the changes of songs, and I don’t play tunes I don’t know, and I know a lot of songs. And I can play piano well enough to comp for my students. So my colleagues are very informed, like Bill Dobbins, and Harold, and Dariusz and Jeff. Jeff is the bass teacher. But they’re very informed. I’m sort of probably the loose cannon of the bunch in terms of theory. I’m not…

When you go against the grain, which I like that term, do you make a specific choice, what’s that going to be? I’m not sure I can be specific about it. If it’s a C9 chord are there formulas to go against the grain with that?
